text: Your push arrives at the exact place where they decide what is worth having. Mars is how you want and how you go and get it. Venus is how they take pleasure, what they find lovely, how regard gets handed out. A conjunction fuses those two, so your appetite and their sense of value end up running on one circuit. The first effect is that you register with them. What you do is never neutral in their company. It either pleases or it grates, and rarely nothing. Effort you consider ordinary reads to them as a kind of style, and when you go after something in front of them they are watching how you do it as much as what you get. That can be flattering. It can also feel like being appraised while you work. What you tend to receive from them is smoothing. They take the raw shape of what you want and give it manners, timing, a better version of itself. Plans of yours come back from them with the sharp corner filed off. If you have spent your life being told you are too much, this is a person in whose company you are not. They find your force agreeable rather than alarming, which is not the usual response and is worth knowing about. What you do to them is less gentle than it looks from your side. You put pressure on their preferences. Taste is the part of a person that likes to take its time, and you are built to move. They may find they agree to things at your speed, then discover a week later that they did not want them at that size or in that order. You are also the person most likely to treat what they enjoy as something to be procured rather than shared. Buying it, arranging it, winning it: those are Mars answers to a Venus question, and they only half work. Anger has a particular flavor here. Because their Venus is on the receiving end, your irritation reaches them as a withdrawal of warmth rather than as a fight. You raise your voice about a schedule and they hear something about whether they are still liked. The message arrives on that channel whether you sent it there or not. The good of this contact is uncomplicated. You supply motion to someone whose instinct is to weigh, and they supply pleasure to someone whose instinct is to press on. Anything with both a task and a taste tends to go well between you: a room, a meal, a trip, an argument that has to be correct and gracious at once. You do the pushing, they do the choosing, and neither of you finds the other's half tedious.

A sextile is a door left open, not a hand on your back. Between your Mars and their Venus it means your drive and their taste can cooperate, provided somebody actually asks. Ask and it goes well. You bring the will to do a thing, they bring an opinion about how it should look or feel or be timed, and the two do not compete for the same ground. Where you would have made a blunt version, their preference improves it at no cost to your momentum. You do not experience their input as interference, which is not something you can say about everyone who has opinions about your work. They tend to enjoy watching you go after things. Your directness entertains them rather than threatening them, and they are inclined to be generous about it. They will smooth over how you said something, praise the part of you other people find abrasive, put in a good word when you are not there. Being liked by this person is easy, and you may notice you never had to earn it twice. They watch you do something they find difficult. Venus is quick to appreciate and slow to pursue, and around you it becomes obvious that a wanted thing can simply be gone after and had. They get slightly braver about their own appetites in your company, more likely to say plainly what they would like instead of arranging the conditions and hoping someone notices. Nothing goes wrong here. What goes wrong is that nothing begins. The two of you can spend years in pleasant proximity without this contact doing any work, because nothing in the geometry forces the issue. Plenty of pairs with this aspect never find out they would have been good at something together. There is also a mild imbalance to watch in the doing. You are the one who moves, and it is easy for that to harden into an arrangement where you carry the effort and they supply the response. That suits both of you right up until it does not. The repair is not complicated: let them originate something occasionally, and take their version at their pace rather than speeding it up on their behalf. Where this shows most plainly is in how trouble ends. Arguments between you rarely harden, since their instinct is to restore good feeling and yours is to get the thing over with, and those two aims point the same direction. You would rather act than sulk. They would rather be pleasant than be right. Between you, most conflict has a short half-life, and that turns out to matter more over years than any amount of initial ease.

You reach, and they want to be approached, and those are not the same act. Your Mars squares their Venus, setting your appetite at a hard angle to their sense of what is graceful. Nobody here is behaving badly. You are being direct and they are being particular, and the two keep landing wrong. Your force reads as coarse to them more often than you intend. You skip the step where a thing is offered and made pleasant, and go for the thing itself. They notice the missing step every single time. From where they stand it can look like you do not care how something is done, when the truth is that you care mostly whether it gets done. They mistake your efficiency for indifference. You mistake their taste for stalling. From your side, their preferences look like conditions nobody wrote down. There is a way they want things timed, phrased, and presented, and you keep tripping over rules you never agreed to. You may find yourself getting loud about small matters, because the small matters seem to be where their objections live. The square also carries heat. Friction between Mars and Venus is not the cold kind: being annoyed by you and being drawn to you are not opposites here, and the same bluntness that makes them wince keeps them paying attention to you. That is part of why the argument does not settle. Neither of you loses interest in it. Daily life shows it in money, in aesthetics, and in pace. What you consider a reasonable expenditure of effort or cash, they consider crude or wasteful in a way they find hard to justify out loud. What they consider worth doing properly, you consider a delay. Shared decisions about how a thing looks, or how much it costs, will surface this faster than any conversation about feelings. The traction is real. This contact teaches you that how you get something is part of what you get, and Mars does not learn that unassisted. It teaches them that an unstated preference is not a preference but a trap. Pairs who work with it stop fighting about the surface and start naming the requirement underneath: you say what you are after, they say what would make it acceptable, and the whole negotiation takes ten minutes instead of three days. None of that removes the grinding. A square keeps its edge for as long as both charts exist. What can change is that the edge stops feeling personal and starts reading as the honest price of two people who run on different rules about desire and delay.

You never have to make a case with this person. Your Mars trines their Venus, and the practical meaning is that what you want tends to land as something they are glad to give. Your effort arrives in a form they already like. Where other people find you too fast, too blunt, or too willing to push, they find you decisive, and that opinion holds even on the days you are being all three. It amounts to a large line of free credit. You spend less energy managing their impression of you than you do with almost anyone, which leaves more for whatever you were actually doing. They get something they cannot easily manufacture alone. Venus can want a thing quietly for years without moving toward it. Your presence makes moving look ordinary. Around you, their preferences turn into plans, and they may notice that projects which had been pleasant fantasies suddenly acquire dates. You are not persuading them of anything. You are just demonstrating that the distance between wanting and having is crossable. In practice this shows up as good chemistry on any job with both a task and a judgment in it: cooking, building, arranging a trip, running an event. You take the parts that need pushing and they take the parts that need choosing, and the handoff happens without discussion. Neither of you treats the other's contribution as the easy half. Nothing here will ever require either of you to change, and that is the whole of the problem. They will not correct your bluntness, because it does not bother them, so you may walk out of their company with a habit intact that costs you dearly elsewhere. You will not slow down, because slowing is never asked for. The ease is genuine, and it is also frictionless the way a wheel carrying no load is frictionless. Because your wanting is so well received here, you can get careless about the difference between what you want and what is good, and they are rarely the one who will point it out. Approval this easy is pleasant and slightly narcotic. What this holds up under is strain. When matters go badly the pattern does not change: you still act, they still find your acting acceptable, and the goodwill needs no repair before either of you can speak. Whatever this bond turns out to be, it is unlikely to go tense over the question of whether you are allowed to want things.

Pursuit at one end, appraisal at the other. Your Mars stands opposite their Venus, so your wanting and their sense of what is worth wanting look straight at each other with the whole chart in between. The usual experience is a polarity that refuses to cancel out. You go after; they consider. You state a preference by acting on it, they state one by declining. Neither of you can quite perform the other's move, and each keeps supplying the half the other left out. That is what an opposition is for, and it is why this one does not go quiet. You will feel appraised around them, and you will not always know the criteria. They are not withholding on purpose. Venus works by attraction rather than by argument, so their yes and their no arrive as atmosphere instead of as a position you can debate. For someone built to push, that is maddening. There is nothing solid to push against. Your directness puts their taste on the spot, and that is the same problem running the other way. They prefer a preference to reveal itself slowly, and you require an answer today. In your company they are forever being asked to commit to something they were still enjoying in the abstract. For some that lands as a relief. Others find it a small violence and say so much later, inside a different argument. Oppositions also pull hard. Whatever this relationship is, the two of you are unlikely to be indifferent to each other. Irritation and interest share a wire in this contact, and it is common to discover that the person who most annoys you is the one whose approval you keep going back for. Neither charge cancels the other, which is why the pattern does not simply wear off. The daily texture is negotiation: how money gets spent, how time gets used, whether a thing should be done now or done well. You will make the case for now. They will make the case for well. Each of you is usually right about the half you are holding, and it only turns sour when one of you starts pretending to hold both. The completion in it is not a compromise. It is that you learn to want something without immediately reaching for it, and they learn that a want with no motion behind it stays a mood. Neither of you gets that lesson from your own chart. You have to face the other person to acquire it, which is precisely what the geometry keeps you doing.

Same make, same tempo, same fuse. Your Mars sits on theirs, so the two of you want and act by one method, and no translation happens between an impulse of yours and an impulse of theirs. The recognition is immediate and physical. You can tell when they are about to move. Their pace is your pace, so being around them costs you nothing in adjustment. You do not slow down for them, wait for them to catch up, or explain why you already started. People with this contact report simply getting on with it together, and that whatever the work is, it goes faster. Side by side you are formidable. Two Marses in one place point the same direction when there is a common object, and shared projects, physical work, deadlines, and any fight against something outside the pair bring out the best of it. Neither of you has to carry the other's share of the push. Turned inward it is a different animal. You provoke each other by the same route you would provoke yourself, so you both know exactly where the sore spot sits and you both reach it at the same speed. Anger goes off fast. Neither of you has the reflex to pause, because the reflex you share is to answer. Arguments climb not because either of you is cruel but because nobody in the room is built to wait. Competition is the other half of it. You go after the same things in the same way, and often the thing you both want is the same thing: the same task, the same recognition, the same place to stand. This rarely gets named out loud. It surfaces as a strange edge in an ordinary conversation, or as your own surprise at how badly you wanted to be the one who finished it. Pacing has its own problem. When you are both tired nothing moves at all, since there is no second engine to start the first. When you are both charged nothing stops. The pair has one gear and you are always in it together. What you can do with this over time is divide the ground. Not chores split evenly, but territory: things that are yours to drive and things that are theirs, settled in advance and honored when tempers are up. The force does not diminish when you do that. It stops being spent on each other and goes into whatever the two of you actually meant to build.

You go about things one way, they go about them another, and the two methods happen to fit. A sextile between your Mars and theirs makes cooperation available on request. It does not turn up unrequested. The practical form: once the two of you agree on an objective, who does which part settles itself in about a minute. You take the parts that suit your kind of push, they take the parts that suit theirs, and neither of you feels shortchanged by the split. Fewer pairs manage that than you might guess. Most pairs argue about method long before they argue about aims. Their energy is easy for you to be near. It does not tire you and it does not draw on the same fuel yours needs. When you are flat, their activity is more likely to interest you than to shame you. When they are stalled, your moving gives them a way in rather than a reason to dig further into the stall. Anger has somewhere to go here, which matters more than it sounds. If something between you has to be had out, it can be had out and then finished, because neither of you is set to escalate on contact and neither is set to disappear. Your disagreements tend to stay about the matter at hand instead of drifting into who is being disrespected. Neither of you will be pushed into using it. Nothing in the contact makes you seek this person out or think to work alongside them. Left alone it is a pleasant compatibility that never gets tested, and many pairs who have it never learn what they could have built. Somebody has to propose. There is also a limit on intensity worth stating plainly. This is not the contact that produces a shared crusade. The two of you are workable rather than fused, and if something between you needs to be urgent, the urgency has to arrive from elsewhere in the two charts or from the situation you are both standing in. Given an actual task, though, the shape of it is plain enough. You get an ally whose effort needs no supervision, no correction, and no matching. You will notice it most on the days when something has to get done and neither of you has the patience for a conversation about who does what.

Two drives at a hard angle, each convinced it is the reasonable one. Your Mars squares theirs, which means you and this person go after what you want by methods that keep obstructing each other. The obstruction is not planned. It is structural, and it repeats. Timing shows it first. You are ready to move when they are not; they start pushing just as you decided to hold. Each of you meets the other at the wrong moment over and over, and after enough repetitions it begins to feel deliberate. It almost never is. Then there is method. You have a way of applying pressure and so do they, and the two do not stack. Where you are direct they may be persistent, or the reverse. The particulars vary, but the effect is that your push does not land on them the way it lands on other people. Whatever normally works for you fails here, which is disorienting, and the usual response is to apply more of it rather than something different. Provocation is the honest word for much of what happens. This person can get a rise out of you cheaply, and you do the same to them. Neither of you necessarily enjoys it, and both of you keep doing it, because the geometry makes the other's ordinary behavior feel like a challenge that needs answering. The traction underneath is genuine, and it is why this contact is worth having rather than only surviving. Nothing between you gets to be lazy. You cannot bulldoze this one, so you are forced to develop a second method, and a second method is exactly what a strong Mars usually lacks. Whatever patience or precision you pick up dealing with them will serve you everywhere else for years. Shared physical work and open competition take a great deal of the edge off. This contact does better with an outside target than with a conversation. Two people who cannot agree about pace can still agree to move a heavy object or finish a job by Friday, and the friction converts into something useful on the way. The failure mode is the standing feud: the same collision, the same words, both of you defending a position instead of stating a want. Say what you are actually after rather than why their approach is wrong, and the argument shortens considerably. None of that files the edge off. It does decide where the edge ends up: on each other, or on the job the two of you are standing in front of.

Effort passes between you without resistance. Your Mars trines theirs, so the way you go after a thing and the way they go after a thing run at compatible angles, and the coordination happens before anybody plans it. The small stuff gives it away. You both reach for the same tool at the same moment and neither of you is annoyed. Work splits itself. Plans made in five minutes turn out to have been enough plan. When you decide to do something with this person, you do not spend the first hour negotiating how it will be done. Their energy tends to restore yours rather than drain it. Some people leave you tired; this one usually leaves you slightly more capable than you arrived. That holds up under strain, which is where trines earn their keep. In a crisis the two of you act in the same direction without checking, and the checking would only have cost time. Conflict is not absent, but it is unusually clean. When you fight, you fight about the thing, and it ends when the thing is settled. Neither of you reads the other's temper as contempt, because the temper looks familiar. It looks like your own. Nobody applies a brake, and the reason is exactly the thing that makes the contact easy. Two Marses in easy contact talk each other into more, faster, sooner, and neither instinct is set to question the direction of travel. If what you are both charging at is a bad idea, this aspect will not say so. It will make the charge more efficient. Pairs with this contact sometimes look back at a decision made at speed and cannot find the moment when either of them could have objected. The second problem is drift. Ease requires nothing, so the contact can sit unused for years and be exactly as available when you finally pick it up again. That is a pleasant property in a friendship and a slightly inert one in a working partnership that needed somebody to insist. What it gives you, plainly, is a person you can act with. Not act like, act with: shared momentum that does not have to be arranged in advance or defended afterward. Whatever else runs complicated between the two of you, the doing of things does not, and the doing of things is a large share of ordinary life.

Face to face, both hands on the same rope. Your Mars opposes theirs, so the drive you carry and the drive they carry point directly at one another, and anything the two of you do together has a contest folded into it. Some of that contest is a pleasure. Opposition is the geometry of the game, and two people pulling opposite ways on one object is what sport, debate, and negotiation are made from. This person may bring out a competitiveness you had forgotten you owned, and you may look forward to it. Being met with equal force is not the same as being obstructed. The rest is less fun. When the two of you want incompatible things, no yielding is built into the geometry. Neither steps aside, because stepping aside is not what one Mars does while looking straight at another. Standoffs can outlast anybody's interest in the original issue. You supply what they omit and they supply what you omit, and that is the useful part. Your way of going after something has a blind spot, and it is standing in front of you wearing their face. If you are fast, they are relentless. If you fight in the open, they wait. Watching them win by a method you would never have used is instructive, as long as you can watch it without hearing a rebuke. Energy level matters too. Oppositions tend to run their two ends alternately: one of you is charged while the other is spent, and then it swaps. That can work nicely, since somebody always has fuel in reserve. It can also mean that the hour you are ready to go is the hour they have just stopped, and the pair keeps missing its window. Anger between you comes in straight. Not sly, not delayed, but aimed. The advantage is clarity, since you generally know where you stand and neither of you has to guess whether something is wrong. The cost is volume, and the cost is real. The completion in this one comes from putting the force somewhere other than each other. Two people who can push this hard, aimed at a common problem, cover ground neither would cover alone. It is the same rope in either case. What differs is whether you are hauling against each other or hauling the same load.

Your appetite has met a person who sees no reason to limit it. Mars conjunct their Jupiter drops what you go after directly onto their sense of scope, belief, and permission, and the meeting is loud. In their company you attempt more. Not because they push you, but because the objection you would ordinarily raise against yourself does not survive contact with their view of the situation. They think the thing is possible. They think you should do it. They frequently think it ought to be bigger. Your ordinary ambition inflates a size or two around them, and you may look back at decisions made in that mood and wonder where your caution went. Some of that is real gain. Jupiter permits, and a person built to press against limits benefits enormously from somebody who does not treat every limit as solid. Confidence you cannot manufacture alone shows up when they are in the room. Work begun under their encouragement often does succeed, because you were probably underestimating yourself and they corrected the figure. Jupiter believes, expands, and holds opinions about the far horizon, and it is not by nature the part of a person that gets up and does anything. You are, and that is your whole contribution here. Their plans acquire a first step when you are near. If they have been talking about a thing for years, you are the one most likely to make it happen this month, and they will be pleased and surprised and slightly rushed. The cost is overshoot, and the brakes are poor in both directions. Effort gets committed on a good afternoon, expense follows the scale of the idea rather than the size of the budget, promises get made about what the two of you will accomplish, and the accounting happens later and somewhere else. Nobody is exaggerating on purpose. The size simply feels correct while you are together. Impatience is the other note. Their sense of how things ought to be can arrive as a sermon, and you were never built to sit through one. When you are already moving, a large view of what your work means can feel like being held up by a lecture. That irritation is better named than swallowed, since swallowed it tends to come back out as speed. Used well, the two of you are excellent at beginnings. You bring the doing, they bring the reason it is worth doing, and between those the thing actually starts. Keeping some part of your own judgment outside the room is the whole discipline this contact asks for.

Bring them a plan and they will find room in it. Your Mars sextiles their Jupiter, an angle that offers rather than insists, so this one pays out when you turn up with something specific. They are useful to you exactly where a project needs permission. You already have the drive. What you often lack is the sense that the larger version is allowed, and they supply that casually, in a sentence, without making a production of it. A conversation with them about something you are working on tends to end with the scope slightly enlarged and you feeling fine about the change. Their optimism gets traction from you, which it does not generate on its own. Jupiter can be satisfied with the idea of a thing. You cannot, and your presence quietly raises the standard, since it is harder to talk about a possibility in front of somebody visibly capable of going and doing it this week. The exchange stays easy at both ends. You do not experience their enthusiasm as pressure, and they do not experience your urgency as rudeness. That combination is worth more in a working relationship than people expect, because it lets the two of you disagree about a plan without either feeling insulted. Nothing here starts on its own. The contact sits unused until somebody names a goal out loud. Two people can be pleasant to each other for a decade and never discover they would have been good at building something. If you want the backing, the introduction, the second opinion about how far to take it, you have to ask. There is a mild version of the usual Jupiter risk here. Encouragement is cheap, and theirs is genuinely cheap: given easily, without much weighing. Their yes is a real yes about what is possible and not always a considered judgment about your particular plan. Take the confidence and do your own arithmetic afterward. In ordinary life this tends to show up as opportunity. They are the one who mentions the opening, passes on the contact, tells you that of course you should apply. Whether anything comes of it depends entirely on whether you move, and the moving was always going to be your half of the arrangement.

You want to get on with it. They want to talk about what it means. Your Mars squares their Jupiter, so your way of going after a thing keeps crossing their sense of how large it should be and what it is for. The everyday form is a mismatch of scale. You arrive with a specific, sized objective and they answer with a bigger frame: what this could become, what it says about the wider situation, why the version you proposed is too modest. If you are already moving, that is not encouragement. It is drag. You brought a task and got a philosophy. They meet something equally unwelcome coming the other way. Your haste looks, from where they stand, like a failure to consider the point. They think you are solving the wrong problem quickly. Whatever principle they hold about how things ought to be done, you walk straight through it, and walking through is not an argument they can get their hands on. Excess is the shared risk, and the blame for it never divides cleanly. Their permission is generous and your appetite is willing, so together you commit to more than either of you would alone: more hours, more expense, more promised to other people. When it goes wrong the accounting turns unpleasant, because each of you can point at the other. They authorized nothing specific and you did all the doing. The friction has a use, and it is not the obvious one. What they force on you is the question of why, which Mars does not ask on its own. Running your effort past somebody who does ask will occasionally stop you from winning something you did not want. What you force on them is cost. Ideas that would have stayed comfortably theoretical get tested against a real attempt, and some of them do not survive it. Arguments about timing will recur for as long as you know each other. They believe there is time. You believe there is not. Neither position is wrong in general and neither of you will convert the other, so what works tends to be procedural rather than philosophical: decide in advance who has the last word on which kind of decision, and the same fight stops being had from scratch every time. What the two of you build under this angle is usually larger than it should be and better than it would have been. Both halves of that are true, and both are worth expecting.

Around this person the road looks wider than it did. Your Mars trines their Jupiter, and the plain result is that your drive finds room in their outlook without having to force anything open. You are believed in without asking. They assume you will manage whatever it is, and the assumption is not flattery. It is simply how the situation looks from where they sit. Confidence like that is contagious, and you may notice yourself taking on things in their vicinity that you would have hesitated over alone. It often works, and it works because their estimate of you was closer to accurate than your own. Their function is not to push you. It is to remove the sense that a thing would be presumptuous. Most people spend a fair share of their energy on the question of whether they are allowed. In this person's company you spend yours on the work instead. What they receive is momentum with nothing unpleasant attached to it. Your acting does not offend their principles and their expansiveness does not slow your acting. Opportunity moves between you in both directions: they mention something, you go and do it, and the credit is easy to share because neither of you gave up much to make it happen. Luck is the folk name for this contact, and it is worth being precise about what it actually is. Nothing here is guaranteed. What the trine provides is that effort spent in their orbit meets less resistance than usual, partly because they open doors and partly because you approach without apologizing first. Nobody in this pair is holding a red pen. They will not tell you the plan is too big, and you will not tell them their optimism carries costs, since between the two of you it has not visibly carried any yet. Enough easy wins and both of you lose the habit of estimating. Any correction that comes will arrive from outside the pair. The plainer risk is comfort. The contact is pleasant enough that you can spend a great deal of time enjoying the sense of possibility and considerably less converting it into anything. Nothing here insists. At its best it is durable and cheap to keep. You give them a reason to expect results, they give you room to try, and neither of you finds the trade costly. What you keep from it is simple enough: near this person your ambition is not a thing that has to be managed.

Your drive holds one end and their sense of scope holds the other, and a good deal of what passes between you is an argument about size. Mars opposite their Jupiter is a contact about scale rather than temperament. The question is not whether to act. It is how far, and how much. You are usually the one holding the specific. You know what you are doing this week and roughly what it will cost. They stand at the far end with the wider view, and from there your objective looks small, or provincial, or beside the point. From your position, their horizon looks like an elegant way of avoiding the work sitting in front of both of you. Neither of you convinces the other, and that failure is the productive part. They pull your effort outward, toward the version of the plan with more in it. You pull their belief back toward something that has a deadline attached. Left to yourselves, you would have done a competent small thing and they would have described a magnificent nothing. Because it is an opposition, the two of you alternate rather than blend. One is expansive while the other is skeptical, and the roles swap without notice. You may find yourself defending caution in one conversation and pressing for more in the next, depending on which end they picked up first. The contact runs hot around risk. Money, commitments, and how much to take on are the recurring subjects, and they will look reckless to you at least as often as you look narrow to them. Two patterns are common and both are avoidable once named: you taking a large action to prove a point about their theory, and them endorsing something extravagant because your practicality got under their skin. There is real generosity in it too. Oppositions are relationships of supply. They give you a reason to attempt something beyond the immediate, which your own drive would never have produced on its own. You give them the experience of a belief being tested where people can see it, which theirs would have preferred to avoid. The grown version of this is division rather than agreement. Let them hold the far end while you hold the near one, and stop treating the other position as an error waiting to be corrected. Two people arguing about how far to go generally get further than one person deciding alone, provided they are still talking by the time the decision is due.
